We use the quotient rule with the numerator $u(x)=\operatorname{ln}⁡x$ and the denominator $v(x)={e}^{2x}.$ 

Differentiating $u(x)$ and $v(x),$ we have

$$
{u}^{′}(x)=\frac{1}{x},\,{v}^{′}(x)=2{e}^{2x}.
$$

Note that we used the chain rule to differentiate $v.$

Now, applying the quotient rule and simplifying, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =\frac{{u}^{′}(x)\cdot v(x)-u(x)\cdot {v}^{′}(x)}{[v(x)]^{2}} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{1}{x})({e}^{2x})-(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)(2{e}^{2x})}{{({e}^{2x})}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{{e}^{2x}}{x}-2{e}^{2x}\operatorname{ln}⁡x)}{{({e}^{2x})}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{{e}^{2x}-2x{e}^{2x}\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{x})}{{({e}^{2x})}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{2x}(1-2x\operatorname{ln}⁡x)}{x{({e}^{2x})}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1-2x\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{x{e}^{2x}}.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
